title: adaptive-ephemeral-reserve-and-fast-fail-stabilizer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an ephemeral reserve layer (hedge bridge) to reduce flapping in regional circuit state and a fast-fail stabilizer that gracefully rejects overloaded requests with improved telemetry; no public API changes.
body:
Context and motivation: Recent incidents (see ENG-4182) revealed oscillation where regional circuit flips caused tenant requests to be retried aggressively, producing cascading latency spikes and SLO violations. This PR introduces an ephemeral 'hedge bridge' reserve and a fast-fail stabilizer to reduce rejoin thrash and make graceful degradation more deterministic. Goal: reduce cross-region reopen flapping, ensure predictable SLO concessions, and provide better telemetry to diagnose transient surges.

What this PR does: 1) Ephemeral reserve: allocate a tiny per-region ephemeral slot pool for hedged requests that would otherwise trigger immediate circuit reopen. The reserve is time-boxed and decays automatically; it lets a small number of requests succeed to probe real capacity without flipping global circuit state. 2) Fast-fail stabilizer: when local load exceeds soft thresholds we now return a deterministic 429-with-reason and telemetry hooks instead of enqueuing indefinite retries; callers receive a short retry-after and a concrete rejection reason allowing client-side backoff. 3) Probe backoff: successful probes from the ephemeral reserve use an exponential probe-success cool-down to avoid rapid re-probing. 4) Telemetry: new metrics (region.hedge.reserve_used, region.hedge.probe_success_rate, region.fastfail.count) and structured log fields for circuit transitions. 5) Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag and enabled by default in canary.

Files and high-level changes: - runtime/hedge_bridge.go: core reserve allocator and decay scheduler. - runtime/circuit_manager.go: integration points for reserve check and transition suppression. - api/errors.go: standardizes 429 payload and retry-after header. - observability/metrics_definitions.yaml: new metrics & dashboards. - tests/*: unit + e2e injecting synthetic region overloads. - docs/operational/hedge-bridge.md: operator notes and rollback steps.

Commits (summary): - init: hedge bridge allocator + tests - integrate: wire into circuit manager and suppress reopen for reserve probes - stabilizer: fast-fail response type and backoff semantics - telemetry: metrics + structured logs + dashboards - tests: flakiness hardening and canary rollout scripts

Testing and CI: Unit tests for allocator logic and probe cooldown added (coverage +8%). E2E scenario simulating regional burst showed 60% reduction in circuit flips and 2x fewer retries across tenants in the canary run. CI: build (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), canary-deploy-check (pass).

Review conversation (high level): - Liam O'Connor: requested clearer invariants around reserve sizing and edge-case where reserve exhaustion could delay legitimate recovery. Author reply: added deterministic decay and max-probe-per-epoch counters; documented behavior in hedge_bridge.go and docs. - Priya Singh: asked for stronger telemetry to link probe events to tenant IDs for postmortem analysis. Author reply: added anonymized tenant buckets and correlation id propagation; confirmed privacy constraints with Security. - Diego Alvarez: asked to ensure fast-fail 429 payload is compatible with SDK retry policies. Author reply: updated api/errors.go to include machine-readable reason and retry_after_secs; coordinated with SDK owners via ENG-4199.

Risk and rollback: The change is feature-flagged and can be disabled per-region. Rollback plan: flip runtime flag to false, which removes reserve allocation and reverts to previous circuit behavior; dashboards and alerting added to detect behavioral regressions within 5 minutes.

Merge outcome: Squash and merge after approvals. Post-merge actions: deploy canary to us-west-2 and eu-central-1 for 24h, monitor region.hedge.probe_success_rate and slo_latencies; coordinate with SRE on incident runbook update.

Related: ENG-4182 (incident), ENG-4199 (SDK coordination), DOCS-112 (operator guide).
